record.paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
record.original_question: Let α_i and λ_i be null sequences with α_i → 0 and λ_i → 0, and for each i let K_i be the middle-α_i Cantor set whose first construction interval is [0, λ_i]. If S is the associated sumset and R_z is the tail set, under what conditions on R_z and on the parameters α_i is S an M-Cantorval, an L-Cantorval, or an R-Cantorval?

evidence.quote:
3. Under what conditions of Rz and αi for i ∈ N will this set be an M-
Cantorval? An L or R Cantorval?

artifact.category_tag: Cantorvals and subsums of null sequences
artifact.status_search_result: A complete characterization of when sumsets of middle-α Cantor sets with α_i → 0 form M-, L-, or R-Cantorvals does not appear in the literature. Related partial progress exists: conditions guaranteeing that the difference set C(λ) − C(λ) of a central Cantor set is a Cantorval (Results in Math. 2023), structural results on arithmetic sums of homogeneous Cantor sets, and characterizations for multigeometric sequences. The general parameter-level classification asked here appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Conditions for the Difference Set of a Central Cantor Set to be a Cantorval
status_evidence.snippet: effective conditions for the sequence λ which guarantee that C(λ) − C(λ) is a Cantorval
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial result on conditions producing a Cantorval, but only for difference sets of a single central Cantor set, not the general sumset classification.

status_evidence.title: On the structure of arithmetic sums of Cantor sets with constant ratios of dissection
status_evidence.snippet: five possible structures for the sum: a Cantor set, a closed interval, or three mixed models called L, R and M-Cantorvals
status_evidence.claim: L/M/R-Cantorvals classified for homogeneous (constant ratio) Cantor sets, but the variable α_i with α_i→0 case is not fully classified.

status_evidence.title: Cantorvals and Subsum Sets of Null Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: subsum set ... is one of: a finite union of compact intervals, a Cantor set, or a symmetric Cantorval
status_evidence.claim: General trichotomy known, but the precise parametric conditions distinguishing M-, L-, R-Cantorvals in this Cantor-set-sum setting are not pinned down.
